title: Latency causality mapping and visual investigation notes
body:
Goal:
Provide a compact operational playbook for mapping causal chains that lead to token/response latency spikes and a set of visual primitives (widgets) to speed triage. This is meant for oncall, SREs, and feature owners who need fast, repeatable investigations across multi-model inference flows.

Context and problem statement:
- We get transient 95th/99th latency spikes that correlate with tenant bursts, cold KV-cache tails, and occasional backend RB failures.
- Existing dashboards show slices but not causality: e.g. high model-forward-latency + high request-queue-depth + sudden KV-cache miss-rate — which of these is the root?
- Need canonical investigation steps and dashboard widgets that make causal links visible without deep ad-hoc queries.

Design principles:
- Anchor to a single request/session id across traces and logs (session_id, request_id). Use a session-replay snippet where available.
- Normalize latency sources to common units (ms/token, ms/request) so stacks add up.
- Use waterfall + heatmap + sankey: show per-hop durations, cold-keyband heat, and routing fanout.
- Prefer small, operator-ready widgets with drill-through to traces.

Canonical investigation flow (quick checklist):
1) Start with the spike window (t0 - 3m, t0 + 3m). Filter to tenant(s) and route(s).
2) Check session-volume: concurrent sessions, queue depth timeseries (per-route). If queue depth increased by >2x at spike, suspect throttling/backpressure.
3) Cross-check KV-cache warmth metric: prefix-warmth %, cold-cache tail distribution. If warm_pct drops and miss latency exists, KV misses likely contributor.
4) Correlate model instance metrics: per-instance token generation latency distribution, GPU utilization, and OOM/eviction logs.
5) Jump to trace anchors: find top 10 traces by aggregated latency in the window and inspect trace waterfall for long remote calls or repeated retries.
6) If retry loops or downstream 503/429 are present, escalate to routing/backend teams and add temporary fallback rule.

Suggested dashboard widgets (compact, operator-first):
- Waterfall-snapshot panel: top N traces in window showing stacked durations (parse, routing, model_infer, kv_lookup, enqueue). Click -> full trace.
- Heatmap: request arrival time vs token index showing per-token latency color (quickly highlights KV miss bands and slow prefix spikes).
- Sankey of routing: ingress -> chosen model variant -> fallback routes (width by count and average latency).
- KV-warmth timeline: warm_pct, cold-miss-rate, median miss latency, with annotations for rolling restarts or cache flush events.
- Queue depth + shed-rate ribbon: shows enqueued request count and number of policy-driven drops (important for graceful degradation analysis).
- Per-tenant latency decomposition table: p50/p95/p99 broken out by subcomponent (enqueue, routing, model, postproc).

Instrumentation/trace design notes:
- Ensure each RPC/span carries tenant_id, route, model_version, kv_key_hash prefix, and session_id. Session_id must be passed to any async worker to re-link traces.
- For long-running multi-token streams, emit periodic 'heartbeat' spans per X tokens with cumulative token index and cumulative duration to enable per-token heatmaps without exploding traces.
- Add an "anchor" span at the start of each request with a property describing routing decision (e.g., routed_via=fast-path|dedicated|fallback).

Sampling & retention tradeoffs:
- Adaptive sampling: keep all traces that cross per-request latency threshold (e.g., >500ms) or contain error codes. 1–5% baseline sampling for normals.
- Store high-fidelity traces for 7 days; keep compact trace index + waterfall aggregates for 30–90 days for trend analysis.

Playbook snippets (quick queries):
- SQL-ish: SELECT session_id, sum(duration) AS total, percentile(duration, 95) FROM spans WHERE timestamp BETWEEN a AND b GROUP BY session_id ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 50
- Heatmap builder: group_by(token_index_bucket, arrival_second) -> median(token_latency)

Unresolved questions / follow-ups:
- How expensive is emitting per-X-token heartbeats at 1X cadence for the busiest tenants? Need SRE perf estimate. (action: Lin to bench token-heartbeat overhead)
- Should we add a derived metric 'causal-score' that heuristically weights KV-miss spikes, queue growth, and retry count to surface likely root causes? (action: Ravi to prototype a scoring rule)
- UX: how to surface fallback routing in the same view without doubling panels? Consider inline annotations in waterfall spans. (action: Maya to mock wireframe)

Immediate action items:
- Instrument 'anchor' span and token-heartbeat in staging by 2024-11-17 (owner: Lin).
- Add waterfall-snapshot and kv-warmth timeline to the operator microdash (owner: Ava, ETA 2024-12-01).
- Prototype causal-score and run on last 30 incident windows (owner: Ravi, ETA 2024-12-08).

Notes and references:
- See CON-4821 for initial incident timelines used to build these heuristics.
- Visual playbook and wireframes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/visual-playbook

Quick operator quickcard (pin to runbook):
- If p99 latency spikes > baseline and queue depth rising: 1) toggle on fallback routing (if configured), 2) inspect kv-warmth for cold tail, 3) open top-10 waterfall traces, 4) escalate if downstream 5xx/429s.

Record of changes:
- 2024-11-03 initial draft (Ava)
- 2024-11-14 added heartbeat instruction and action owners (Lin)
- 2025-01-09 review with SRE, clarified sampling guidance (Ravi)

Open commentary welcome — this is intentionally compact; if you need a longer deep-dive with sample queries and Grafana/Tempo panels export, I can add another appendix with example JSON panel definitions.
